name: Adobe Acrobat
whyPeoplePay: Acrobat is the reference implementation of the PDF specification, written by the company that wrote the specification, and that shows up in the boring places: a form that fills correctly on a phone, an OCR pass that gets a scanned invoice right the first time, and a signature a bank's compliance desk has seen before. You are paying for the file opening the same way on somebody else's machine.

plans.name: Acrobat Reader
plans.note: Free. Reads, prints and comments. It does not edit, combine, compress, OCR or redact, which is the boundary the paid tiers sell.

plans.name: Acrobat Standard
plans.note: Month-to-month, one person. About $14.99/mo on an annual plan paid monthly, which locks you in for a year.

plans.name: Acrobat Pro
plans.note: Month-to-month, one person. About $19.99/mo on an annual plan paid monthly. Adds redaction, PDF comparison and the advanced form and accessibility tooling.

pricing.note: TODO: re-read the vendor page and raise this confidence. Adobe's own pricing page timed out twice on 2026-08-05, so these figures come from our own recent knowledge of the US list price and were only cross-checked against secondary price trackers, not read off adobe.com. We record the month-to-month figure rather than the annual-paid-monthly one because the cheaper number is a twelve-month commitment with an early-cancellation fee, and savings math built on it overstates what someone on a rolling plan is actually giving up. Regional prices differ; this row is USD only.

ranked.rationale: The only one here that covers the whole boring middle of Acrobat, splitting, merging, rotating, compressing, OCR and form flattening, from a single container with no database behind it. It is a toolbox rather than an editor: it will not let you retype a paragraph inside a page the way Acrobat Pro does, and the page says so before you install it.
